task_description: Write a method in Dafny that takes in an array and an integer L and splits the given array into two parts where the length of the first part of the array is L, and returns the resulting array in a sequence.
specification_response:
Method Signature:
    method SplitArrayAtL(a: array<int>, L: nat) returns (result: seq<int>)
Postconditions_prompt:
    - The length of the resulting sequence should be equal to the length of the input array
- The first L elements of the sequence should correspond to the first L elements of the array
- The remaining elements of the sequence should correspond to the elements of the array starting from position L
- The sequence should contain all elements of the array in their original order, partitioned at position L
code_response:
Step 1: Determine the method’s signature.
In this case:
    method SplitArrayAtL(a: array<int>, L: int) returns (result: seq<int>)
    
Step 2: Determine the preconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - The input array should not be null
    - The value L should be within the array bounds (0 <= L <= a.Length)
    
Dafny specification:
    requires a != null
    requires 0 <= L <= a.Length
    
Step 3: Determine the postconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - The resulting sequence contains the first L elements of the array followed by the remaining elements
    - The length of the resulting sequence is equal to the length of the array
    - The sequence preserves the order of elements from the array
    
Dafny specification:
    ensures result == a[..L] + a[L..]
    ensures |result| == a.Length
    
Step 4: Write the code, its formal specification, and the verification annotations that help the solver prove the postconditions.
In this case:

```dafny
method SplitArrayAtL(a: array<int>, L: int) returns (result: seq<int>)
    requires a != null
    requires 0 <= L <= a.Length
    ensures result == a[..L] + a[L..]
    ensures |result| == a.Length
{
    var resSeq := seq<int>{};
    var i := 0;
    while i < a.Length
        invariant 0 <= i <= a.Length
        invariant resSeq == a[..i]
        decreases a.Length - i
    {
        resSeq := resSeq + seq<int>{a[i]};
        i := i + 1;
    }
    result := resSeq;
}
```
